absent: Behavior of arch kexec allocation, relocation, cleanup and hotplug hooks beyond their declared presence.
Semantics of lookup_address, change_page_attr_set_clr, flush_tlb_one_kernel, set_pte and TLB ordering guarantees.
Definitions and widths of PAGE_SIZE, PG_LEVEL_4K, _PAGE_PRESENT, PTE_PFN_MASK and __pte_needs_invert.
Layout and population of KFENCE pool, cpu_entry_area arrays and KMSAN shadow versus origin contents.
Meanings of CPU_ENTRY_AREA_BASE, CPU_ENTRY_AREA_SIZE, phys_base, KERNEL_IMAGE_SIZE, PAGE_OFFSET and boot_cpu_data fields.
Caller contexts, locking beyond preemption control, and fault handling after lazy KFENCE protection.
Stack-top source, template symbols and encoding details for optimized probes and emulation callbacks.
Expansion of KVM_ARCH_REQ, request wait versus no-wakeup mechanics and handling per request number.
Numeric values of BIT and BIT_ULL positions, PG_LEVEL constants, PAGE_SHIFT and segment selector enumeration values.
Ownership and update rules for kvm_caps, host values, MMU roles, rmap heads and root history.

findings.text: Kexec 64-bit entry context stores complete general purpose state as wide unsigned integers including accumulator through extended registers plus stack pointer, frame pointer and instruction pointer in declaration order.

Architecture declares provision of kexec and crash hooks for page allocation completion, pre-free handling, crash reservation protection changes, relocation application, image post-load cleanup and hotplug event handling.
Crash core header size query resolves to architecture specific implementation through a macro alias.

KFENCE pool initialization iterates over the pool page by page while addresses belong to the pool, fails if any address lacks a page table mapping, demotes non-small mappings to small pages, and reports overall success.
Small-page conversion helper forwards an address and page count to a generic page attribute change routine requesting the small-page attribute set with no attributes cleared.

KFENCE page protection resolves the entry for one address, returns early when already in the requested present state, otherwise toggles presence through a speculation guard and reports success as boolean.
Protection path warns and fails when the lookup yields no entry or when the mapping level is not a small page, so callers must only pass mapped small KFENCE pages.

Unprotecting a page to present needs no TLB maintenance, while protecting to non-present flushes only the local CPU without cross-CPU IPIs because the path may run with interrupts disabled and tolerates stale remote entries.
Local TLB invalidation for KFENCE protection is bracketed by suppression of preemption around the single-entry kernel flush.

Two builds of the protection-none guard differ: one returns the new value unchanged, the other inverts the masked frame portion when none-ness changes between old and new values to hinder speculation.
KGDB transport buffer holds 1024 bytes, breakpoint instruction occupies one byte, cache flush is declared safe, and breakpoint offset correction is delegated to the debugger.

32-bit KGDB register ordering starts with classic general registers through index registers then instruction pointer, flags and six segment selectors, with origin identifier 41, sixteen registers total and byte size derived from register count times word width.

64-bit KGDB ordering covers base general registers plus eight extended registers then instruction pointer, flags and segment selectors, with origin identifier 57, twenty-four registers total and byte size combining seventeen wide slots plus five narrow slots.
Breakpoint helper issues a single trap instruction to enter the debugger.

KMSAN metadata lookup accepts only addresses inside the per-CPU entry area window, derives CPU number and offset, rejects out-of-window offsets, then returns the per-CPU shadow or origin slot selected by a flag.
Physical address validity is unconditional without wide physical addresses, otherwise it requires no bits above the CPU reported physical width.

Virtual address validity distinguishes kernel image mapping from page-offset mapping by unsigned subtraction behavior, adjusts to a physical value, enforces image size and physical validity bounds, then tests frame validity.
Frame validity test suppresses preemption and re-enables it without rescheduling to avoid recursion through scheduler paths under instrumentation.

Probe opcode is an unsigned byte, stack sampling is bounded by 64 bytes with helpers measuring depth from stack top and clamping to that bound, and instruction slot flush is defined as having no effect.
Optimized probe length bound adds maximum instruction size and displacement width, while total optimized size adds template span plus that bound plus jump instruction width.

Architecture probe instruction holds original copy pointer, single-bit boost state, size byte, opcode union distinguishing conditional branch type, loop type with address size, and indirect register form, plus relative offset, emulate callback and poked length.
Optimized probe instruction holds a small fixed copied-instruction area sized by displacement width, a detour buffer pointer and the copied size.
Optimized probe readiness is reported by returning the stored copied size as an integer.
Probe nesting state records outer probe pointer, status and flag snapshots, while per-CPU control block records current status and flags plus one saved nesting record.
Default probe debug handler ignores its register context and returns zero.

KVM virtual CPU limits use a configurable maximum with a 1024 fallback, an identifier ratio of four producing maximum identifiers as product, three internal memory slots, a default halt poll of two hundred thousand nanoseconds, interrupt pins tied to IOAPIC pin count, and manual dirty logging combining protect-enable with initially-set.

First group of architecture virtual CPU requests occupies sequential numbers starting at zero and covers timer, TPR, fault, MMU, clock, page directory, event, page-fault halt, steal time, NMI, PMU, PMI and SMI functions.

Extended request numbers continue sequentially and a subset carries wait semantics with most also suppressing wakeup, covering master clock, IOAPIC scan, APIC reload, hypervisor services, TLB flushes, interrupt maps, nested state, logging and protected-state updates.
Invalid page is defined as all bits set and validity means inequality with that sentinel.

Huge page support spans from small-page level to one-gigabyte level with derived counts, shifts, sizes, masks and pages-per-entry relations, plus limits of 256 CPUID entries, eight variable MTRRs, sixty-four async faults per virtual CPU and four debug registers.

Virtual CPU register enumeration covers general registers with extra registers on 64-bit, then instruction pointer, page directory pointers, control registers with return-predictor aliasing, flags, segments and exit info fields ending in a total count.
Fast-path exit handling distinguishes no fast handling, re-entry to guest, handled exit and exit to userspace as four ordered outcomes.

Page fault error encoding uses low bits for present, write, user, reserved, fetch, protection key and shadow stack plus a high bit for enclave faults, with wider guest bits for reverse-map, final versus page stage, encryption, size mismatch and privilege level.
Two synthetic fault bits mark implicit accesses and private accesses, and their union forms a synthetic mask.
Capability record reports timer control and scaling parameters, bus-lock and notify exit support, VM type mask, and supported masks for machine check, extended state, performance, EFER and quirks.
Host values record raw physical address width independent of repurposed bits plus host EFER, extended state components, shadow CET and architecture capabilities.

MMU page role packs level, guest entry width, quadrant, directness, access, invalidity, NX, write-protect, SMI suppression, dirty tracking, guest mode, passthrough, mirror and SMEP flags with system-management mode occupying the top byte for shift extraction.

Extended MMU role records validity plus executable-only, paging extension, protection keys, supervisor map, five-level paging, long mode and fetch-fault behavior, and CPU role combines base plus extended views addressable as one 64-bit value.
Reverse mapping head is a single atomic value and programmed I/O request carries transfer count, direction, port and access width.
Page format describes reserved-bit masks per level, bad memory-type combination, protection-key mask and a sixteen-entry permission table indexed by fault-code subset.

MMU root info pairs guest and host page roots with an invalid sentinel using invalid pages for both, supports three previous roots, and encodes current, indexed previous and all-roots selections as bit masks while declaring reader-writer lock support.
